title: Tests: harness and toolchain
summary: The harness and toolchain tests cover 20 files and about 4,240 lines. The harness profile runs 290 tests in about 26 s, and tests/toolchain adds 36 more. The tests focus on behaviour and say honestly what kind of evidence they give. They drive hooks and CLIs at the process boundary with fakes on PATH, and they cover DH-05's whole hook fixture list. Keep unittest. The harness profile runs `python3.12 -m unittest discover` in a reduced environment before any bootstrap, and judge_unittest parses unittest's summary to refuse empty or skipped suites. pytest exists only in the service venv, so switching would tie the harness to bootstrap. The gains come from modern unittest habits (enterContext, subTest, a shared base and support module), not from a new runner. Two guards do not guard. The private run-column check reads only the first grant of the first runs migration, while five later migrations add grants to the same role. The offline pin and launcher tests in tests/toolchain run in no profile, though they pass in 0.08 s. The two largest files are arranged by when tests were added, not by what they test. test_hooks.py is one 45-test class covering seven subjects in 703 lines. test_assistant_assets.py packs eight suites and about 165 lines of checker code into 783 lines. Fixture plumbing (stub executables, Git repositories, config roots, report records) is rewritten in each file, and the Git setups are hardened differently. Failures are hard to read: 47 of 60 `assertTrue(any(...))` calls carry no message. Fourteen child processes have no timeout, under one 60-second cap for the whole suite. Five tests assert source text rather than behaviour. No lint or format configuration covers these files: the service's own ruff rules report 456 issues, and 20 of 20 files would be reformatted. test_evidence.py, test_specs.py and test_verify_profiles.py are over 300 lines but each tests one module. They need shared helpers, not splitting.

scores.why: No lint, format or type configuration covers these files; the service's own ruff rules give 456 findings, 20 of 20 files would be reformatted, and two quote styles and two import orders coexist.
About 165 lines of checker code live in a test module beside a second frontmatter parser in harness_lib; tests/toolchain has a support module but tests/harness has none.
No function exceeds 40 lines, but test_hooks.py and test_assistant_assets.py each pack six to eight subjects into 700 to 780 lines.
Helpers are short builders with one job each; a few tests run several phases while their names describe only the first.
Files follow when tests were added (test_final_review.py, appended classes) rather than the unit under test; fingerprint and config_errors tests are spread over three files.
unittest suits the install-free harness; tests run at the process boundary with fakes on PATH and mutate one valid baseline, though some assert source text and some are lint rules in disguise.
Module docstrings state the evidence class and its limits, and comments explain why; a few test names promise more than the test checks.
Helpers are partly annotated (bare dicts, untyped callbacks) and no type checker runs on them; the run-state oracle is a hand copy instead of the generated contract.
Error paths of the code under test are covered thoroughly, but 14 child processes have no timeout and a hang shows up as an anonymous suite error.
Strong behavioural coverage of DH-05's fixture list, weakened by a grant guard that misses later migrations, unwired static guards, unreadable failure messages and one order-dependent test.
Each test reads well on its own, but extending the suite is costly: fixtures are duplicated, two files are oversized and no style is enforced.

strengths.title: One valid baseline, one change, one exact error
strengths.evidence: valid_root in tests/harness/test_assistant_assets.py:173-198 is documented as making 'each negative fixture change one thing', and tests built on it assert the exact error list (test_assistant_assets.py:306, :313). test_evidence.py:77-112 builds valid_manifest from the real template, and its rejected() helper prints the error list on failure. test_disposable_guard.py:61-77 and test_supabase_stack.py:69-89 use named one-line mutators, with change.__name__ as the subTest label.

strengths.title: DH-05's hook fixture list is covered at the process boundary
strengths.evidence: tests/harness/test_hooks.py covers malformed JSON (170-176), the input cap at its exact boundary (188-194), unsupported events and tools without echo (290-299), the deadline (301-311), a missing library (319-327), symlink loops and unusable paths (339-346), secret names before and after links (348-358), and shell metacharacters kept as data (360-377).

strengths.title: Fakes on PATH show that refusals happen before any side effect
strengths.evidence: test_disposable_guard.py:80-113 puts a recording fake docker on PATH and asserts it was never called. test_assistant_assets.py:438-444 shows the version probe inherits no credential. test_hooks.py:578-592 shows Git is asked only when an edit needs it. test_verify_profiles.py:121-126 makes find_tools raise if it is looked up.

strengths.title: Docstrings say honestly what kind of evidence each suite gives
strengths.evidence: test_hooks.py:1 says 'not proof of Claude event delivery', test_verify_profiles.py:1 says they 'prove no real toolchain run', and test_evidence.py:1 says they 'qualify no real work item'. test_non_mutating.py:1-6 classifies each result as disposable, mock or static, and test_reproducible.py:1-5 says 'Neither absence is a skip'.

strengths.title: unittest suits the install-free harness, and the runner refuses empty or skipped suites
strengths.evidence: scripts/verify.py:84-101 runs stdlib unittest in a reduced environment with no bootstrap. judge_unittest fails a suite that is empty or skips a test, and test_verify_profiles.py:260-283 tests that judgement itself.

strengths.title: Readable fixture builders and one shared arrangement
strengths.evidence: test_specs.py:21-70 builds stories and documents with keyword-argument builders (story(), document()). forward_arrangement.py:45-96 is used by both the runbook and ArrangementTests. Each anchor must match exactly once, and the copy is built beside its destination, so a failed run leaves nothing behind.

strengths.title: tests/toolchain/support.py is the pattern to spread
strengths.evidence: support.py:20-35 centralises paths and constants, :56-62 builds a credential-free environment, and :86-107 owns the copy lifecycle with guarded removal. Test modules import `from support import REPO_ROOT, toolchain` (test_manifests.py:14), and setUpClass cleans up when bootstrap fails (test_non_mutating.py:83-90, test_reproducible.py:27-37).

strengths.title: Test names and comments say what is tested and why
strengths.evidence: Names read as sentences, such as test_hooks.py:459 test_a_forged_cwd_never_chooses_a_root_outside_the_home_checkout. Comments explain why, at test_hooks.py:51 ('Naming a key isn't reading it.'), :352-355 and :605, and test_assistant_assets.py:364.

findings.title: Private run-column guard reads only the first grant of one migration

locations.note: Reads 20261105000002_runs.sql only, and re.search keeps the first grant
A later column grant to authenticated on public.runs that the guard never reads
Another later grant the guard never reads
The db profile denies lease_generation at runtime; nothing checks checkpoint_thread_id

findings.evidence:
Five later migrations (…0003:19, …0007:7, …0012:3, …0014:34, …0023:30) add `grant select (...) on public.runs to authenticated`, and the test reads none of them. A table-level grant would also pass, because the pattern needs a column list.
text = (ROOT / app_db.MIGRATIONS / '20261105000002_runs.sql').read_text()
grant = re.search(r'grant select \(([^)]*)\) on public\.runs to authenticated', text)
self.assertNotIn('lease_generation', grant[1])
self.assertNotIn('checkpoint_thread_id', grant[1])
findings.impact: The test is named to promise that the private lease and checkpoint columns never reach the authenticated role. Yet a forward migration that grants checkpoint_thread_id passes it, and the db profile's runtime probe covers only lease_generation. So drift at the grant boundary, which this guard exists to catch, goes unseen.
findings.recommendation: Scan every migration in name order for column-level and table-level grants on public.runs to authenticated. Collect the granted columns and assert they never include the private set or a table-level grant. Add a known-bad fixture (a later grant of checkpoint_thread_id) to show the scan fails on it. Separately, ask the owner of scripts/app_db.py to add a checkpoint_thread_id denial beside the lease_generation case.
findings.ruleCheck: AGENTS.md and .claude/rules/database.md say migrations only move forward. The fix only reads migrations and edits none. It makes a guard stronger and leaves the db profile's runtime role checks in place.
findings.verifierNote: Verified: the test reads only 20261105000002_runs.sql, and five later migrations grant run columns to authenticated. None grants a private column today. app_db.py:208-209 denies only lease_generation at runtime, and no db check reads checkpoint_thread_id as authenticated.

findings.title: Static pin and launcher guards in tests/toolchain run in no profile

locations.note: toolchain_scope_tests discovers only test_scaffold_scope.py
15 offline pin, lock and runbook tests; run read-only here, all pass in 0.08 s
The static N7 launcher ban shares a module with tests that need registry downloads
check_steps relies on it: 'Tests scan this list for install launchers'
The runbook relies on test_manifests.py to catch a pin it does not name
Precedent: an unwired toolchain test broke and nobody noticed

findings.evidence: verify.py builds Step('toolchain_scope_tests', (..., 'unittest', 'discover', '-s', 'tests/toolchain', '-p', 'test_scaffold_scope.py'), root). Its comment says 'Its copies bootstrap from registries, so the rest stays manual'. But test_manifests.py makes no copy: it only reads pyproject.toml, the package.json files, both locks and the runbook. `python3.12 -I -B -m unittest discover -s tests/toolchain -p test_manifests.py` ran 15 tests in 0.079 s, all passing, and wrote nothing. The N7 Launchers class is static too. Nothing else checks that manifests hold exact pins: toolchain check verifies lock freshness and runtime pins, not dependency ranges.
findings.impact: A `^` range in apps/web/package.json with a matching lock, an unqualified dependency bump, or a new `npx` or `uv run` in a package script passes harness, fast and full. DH-09's ban on download-at-runtime launchers and the runbook's pin procedure rest on tests that run only when someone remembers. US-1.8 already records this failure mode for the scope test.
findings.recommendation: Run the offline toolchain modules in the existing scope step. Move the N7 Launchers class into its own module, and give the offline modules one filename pattern that the step discovers, or list them explicitly. Because they take under a tenth of a second, consider running them in fast as well as full. Add a harness test that fails when a tests/toolchain module is neither matched by that pattern nor on an explicit manual list. Correct the verify.py comment and the development-harness runbook line that say the rest needs registries.

findings.evidence: The file is 703 lines with one class. By subject it holds: PreToolUse guard 6, Stop 1, report freshness and fingerprints 9 (harness_lib), hook-settings config_errors 3 (harness_lib), dispatcher process contract 6, PostToolUse diagnostics 3, worktree session roots and Git failures 16, and verify.py 1. 39 of the 45 tests open their temporary directory inline (`with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as ...: root = Path(...)`). The class grew by appending: commit 9a9b60a alone added 277 lines of worktree tests.
findings.impact: To find the tests for a function you search a 700-line class. Because 13 of the tests exercise harness_lib or verify.py, a fingerprinting change has tests here, in test_verify_profiles.py and in test_final_review.py. Each new hook behaviour lands in the same class, and the repeated temp-directory block adds an indentation level and two lines to almost every test.
findings.recommendation: Split by unit under test into focused modules that share a harness support module. Move the harness_lib and verify.py tests to their own modules. Give each class a setUp that uses `self.enterContext(tempfile.TemporaryDirectory())` (Python 3.11+) instead of a with-block in every test.

findings.evidence: The file has 783 lines, 8 classes and 53 tests. They cover rule links, the AGENTS.md mapping, assistant adapter status, activation refusals, the verify report, real instruction assets, the ingestion grammar and the forward arrangement. Lines 75-240 hold the frontmatter parser and policy, the link checker, a hand-written glob matcher, the grammar check, the synthetic root builder, the stub writers and the specs CLI wrapper. findings.title: Instruction-file checks live in a test module beside a second frontmatter parser

locations.note: frontmatter() and frontmatter_errors(): allowed keys, name matches path, model must be inherit
broken_links(): link and fragment resolution
rule_globs() and a hand-written glob matcher
ingestor_grammar_errors()
config_errors parses frontmatter again, in a different way

findings.evidence:
A missing name or description is a named project_configuration error. Allowed keys, the name-to-path match and `model: inherit` are checked only by unittest assertions on the real tree (test_assistant_assets.py:594-597). The two readers split the header differently:
# test_assistant_assets.py:79
header = text[4:].split('\n---\n', 1)[0]
# scripts/harness_lib.py, inside config_errors
header = text.split('---', 2)[1]
if not any(line.startswith('name:') for line in header.splitlines()):
findings.impact: Two readers of the same frontmatter can disagree: harness_lib's split ends the header at the first '---' anywhere, even inside a value, while the test's reader needs a line of its own. A policy violation shows up as a failing test inside harness_behavior_tests, not as a named project_configuration error in the report. And because only the test calls these checks, no skill or other validator can reuse them.
findings.recommendation: Move the eight functions into scripts, in harness_lib or a scripts/instruction_checks.py that it imports. Share one frontmatter parser, and have config_errors report their errors. Keep the known-good and known-bad fixtures as tests. Point those tests at the moved functions before switching config_errors over.

findings.title: Three hook tests' names and assertions disagree

locations.note: Named 'without echo', but only the deny decision is asserted
Named 'does not execute command input', but mostly asserts the command denylist
Named 'never claims live proof', but the reason is never read
The denial reason is a fixed string today, so 'no echo' holds only by construction

findings.evidence:
test_stop_blocks_once_and_never_claims_live_proof asserts only `response['decision'] == 'block'` and that the retry carries no decision. The secret-file test asserts only the deny decision:
def test_secret_files_rejected_without_echo(self):
    ...
        response = hook.handle(root, {'hook_event_name': 'PreToolUse',
                                     'tool_name': 'Read', 'tool_input': {'file_path': name}})
        self.assertEqual(response['hookSpecificOutput']['permissionDecision'], 'deny')
findings.impact: A change that puts the path into the denial reason, or drops Stop's statement that it certifies nothing, still passes the tests named after those guarantees. When the mixed test fails, its name points at the wrong behaviour.
findings.recommendation: Assert what each name promises. For each secret name and command, assert `name not in reason` inside a subTest. Read Stop's reason and assert it says the hook certifies no completion. Move the denylist cases out of the non-execution test into their own test driven by subTest.

findings.title: Fourteen child processes have no timeout under a shared 60-second cap

locations.note: One timeout=60 covers the whole harness suite; on expiry only 'TimeoutExpired' is kept
One of 8 specs.py runs in this file without a timeout
git in setUp without a timeout, run for each of 28 tests
/bin/sh running Makefile lines, no timeout
specs.py render with no timeout
git with no timeout while setting up a copy
specs_cli: the same call, with timeout=30

findings.evidence: An ast scan of the 20 files finds 14 subprocess.run calls with no timeout argument, 8 of them in test_specs.py. The harness reports from 2026-11-12 ran 290 tests in 25.4 to 26.6 s against verify.py's `timeout=60`. When that timeout expires, run_check records status 'error' with output 'TimeoutExpired' and exits 2 ('could not run'), discarding everything the suite printed.
findings.impact: A hang in any of these children, such as Git waiting on a prompt or a regression in specs.py, uses up the whole budget. It then shows as an error that names no test, and the Stop hook blocks on a missing harness pass. As stories add more process-level tests, the suite creeps toward the cap and nothing shows which tests cost most.
findings.recommendation: Route every child process through one support helper, `run_cli`, with a default timeout of 30 s (as specs_cli already uses), so a hang fails the test that caused it. Ask the scripts owner to add unittest's `--durations 10` (Python 3.12) to the harness command and to keep the tail of partial output when the suite times out.
findings.ruleCheck: DH-05 asks for deadlines and bounded output, and DH-09 never counts a timed-out check as green. Per-test timeouts turn an anonymous suite error into a named failure.
findings.verifierNote: Recounted 14 subprocess.run calls without a timeout; the one Popen waits with timeout=10. The newest harness report, written after the reviewer read the 15:53Z one, ran the same 290 tests in 25.4 s, so the evidence now cites both. The 60-second cap and the discarded output are as cited (verify.py:67-73).

findings.title: Config roots and harness reports are built four ways, which weakens assertions

locations.note: valid_root: a complete synthetic root, so one change gives one error
Partial root built inline; asserts a count of matching errors
The same inline root; asserts with any()
A third inline root; asserts with any()
valid_report

findings.evidence: The inline roots in test_hooks.py copy autobots.json and settings.json but create no rules, skills, agents or AGENTS.md. config_errors therefore returns many unrelated errors, so those tests can only check `any('only the reviewed hooks' in error ...)` or count matches. Tests built on valid_root assert the exact list instead, e.g. `self.assertEqual(config_errors(self.root), ['AGENTS.md: missing the "## Rule checks and review" section.'])` (test_assistant_assets.py:306). The three passing harness check records are typed out twice, at test_hooks.py:30-33 and test_verify_profiles.py:21-23.
findings.impact: The inline-root tests would still pass if the edit also caused a second, wrong error. Any change to the report schema or to the required checks has to be made in four builders.
findings.recommendation: Move valid_root, valid_agents and edit_json into the support module, and rebuild the three test_hooks.py cases on valid_root with exact-list assertions. Provide one `harness_report(root, **overrides)` builder for test_hooks.py, test_verify_profiles.py and test_evidence.py.
findings.ruleCheck: DH-09 asks the harness for known-good and known-bad checker fixtures. One valid baseline per check makes each known-bad case differ by exactly one change.
findings.verifierNote: Verified: the inline roots at test_hooks.py:139-168 and 329-337 copy only autobots.json and settings.json, so their tests count or any() matches, while the valid_root tests assert exact lists (test_assistant_assets.py:306 and 313); the three passing records are typed twice.

findings.evidence: The service's own rules (E, F, W, I, B, UP, ASYNC, RUF; line length 100), run isolated over tests/harness and tests/toolchain, give 456 findings. 431 are E501, and 132 remain even at 120 columns. findings.title: N4 only works if it runs last against a shared prepared copy

locations.note: Docstring: 'Test names set the order: drift goes last'

edit() already restores by bootstrapping again

findings.evidence: PreparedCopy bootstraps one copy in setUpClass. test_zz_n4 runs `uv pip uninstall idna` and leaves the environment drifted. It relies on unittest's alphabetical method order to run last.
findings.impact: Running with -k, under a runner that reorders tests, or after adding a test whose name sorts after zz, gives later tests a drifted environment, so they fail for the wrong reason.
findings.recommendation: Restore the environment in a cleanup, as edit() does for pyproject changes (`self.addCleanup(support.bootstrap_copy, self.root)`), and drop the zz prefix. Alternatively, give N4 its own class and its own copy.
